issues.legal_issue: On release of requisitioned property, possession is ordinarily to be given to the person from whom it was taken, without determining that person’s antecedent title.
material_facts: The property was requisitioned by a written order addressed to the person then in possession, and possession was taken from that person.
Before release from requisition, the government had not formally or symbolically taken possession of the property from that person.
The release order specified a government department as the recipient of possession.
issues.conclusion: The release inquiry under Section 35(1) concerns events after requisition that may affect who should receive possession; ordinarily, possession should be returned to the person from whom it was taken. The inquiry does not extend to determining competing antecedent title, and delivery under Section 35(2) does not prejudice rights enforceable through due process of law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 29(2) of the Defence of India Act, 1962, requisition may be effected by an order served on the person deemed to be the owner or person in possession. Section 35(1) provides for specifying the person to whom possession is to be given on release, as far as practicable the person appearing entitled to possession at that time. The inquiry under Section 35(1) is summary and is concerned with relevant events after requisition, not adjudication of antecedent title. Section 35(2) makes delivery a discharge of the government’s liabilities without prejudicing rights enforceable by due process of law. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.requisition_release_proceeding: The matter concerns who should receive possession when requisitioned property is released.
predicates.possession_taken_from_person: The authorities took possession of the property from a person when it was requisitioned.
predicates.no_post_requisition_event_changes_entitl: No event after requisition occurred that changes who should receive possession on release.

issues.definition: When a release proceeding concerns property taken from a person and no later event changes entitlement to possession, possession is returned to that person.

issues.legal_issue: A person whose possession was taken on requisition may receive conditional relief on appeal even though the person’s allotment was provisional, where the government had not retaken possession before requisition.
material_facts: The appellant was put in possession under a provisional allotment that required final government approval, which was never given.
The allotment had been cancelled, but the government had not recovered possession before the property was requisitioned from the appellant.
The appeal challenged the refusal to direct delivery of possession to the appellant after release from requisition.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed in part: the government was directed to deliver possession to the appellant unless, within the specified period, it took adequate and lawful steps to retake formal possession. The government could also seek recovery later, and an aggrieved party could pursue the statutory process for determining rights.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Sections 29 and 35 of the Defence of India Act, 1962, the Court treated the person from whom possession had been taken as the proper recipient on release, while recognizing that the provisional allotment did not establish a final entitlement to the property. In exercising its jurisdiction under Article 136, the Court fashioned conditional relief on the particular facts rather than an unconditional order.

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal brought by special leave against the refusal of relief concerning possession.
predicates.possession_taken_from_appellant: The authorities took the property’s possession from the appellant when it was requisitioned.
predicates.allotment_only_provisional: The appellant’s allotment was provisional and had not received final approval.
predicates.government_had_not_retaken_possession_be: The government had not recovered possession from the appellant before the requisition occurred.

issues.definition: In a special-leave appeal with these possession and provisional-allotment facts, the appellant receives a conditional direction for possession.

issues.legal_issue: A post-release allotment of the property to another person may justify refusing an order directing the government to recover possession for the former possessor.
material_facts: The property was requisitioned from the appellant and later released from requisition.
After release, the government took possession and allotted the property to another person.
The appellant sought an order requiring the government to return possession and to displace the new allottee.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was dismissed; the Court declined to direct the government to take steps to complete the formal recovery of possession or to dispossess the new allottee.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 35(1) and 35(2) of the Defence of India Act, 1962, release entails specifying a recipient for possession, while rights in the property remain enforceable through due process of law. On the special facts, the Court declined to grant the requested relief in its jurisdiction under Article 136 because the property had already been allotted to another person after release. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal brought by special leave seeking possession after requisitioned property was released.

issues.definition: When an appeal for possession follows requisition and release, and the property has since been allotted to another person, the appeal is dismissed without an order displacing that person.
